Nord-Kivu (page 7): 471 hospitalized, 2 critical; 349 in CTE/CT for 410 beds (printed 85.1%), suspects 178/192 (92.7%) and confirmed 171/218 (78.4%); 122 in facilities that are not CTE/CT (printed 26%; 122/471 is 25.9%). 349+122=471 reconciles. Hot meals went to 177 confirmed and 194 suspects, which do not match the 171/178 split; not used.
Haut-Uele: 39 confirmed cases hospitalized; 2 confirmed deaths and 2 non-case exits at the Pawa CTE; admissions and occupancy not transmitted.
Tshopo: 19 patients for 36 beds (52.8%); 2 suspect admissions and 1 exit (escape); 6 confirmed cases from Bafwasende lost to follow-up.
Bas-Uele: 3 patients in isolation; no new confirmed case, recovery or death.
challenges: Contacts 28144/35162 (80.0%), up from 79.1% but below the 95% threshold; 7018 unseen (20.0%). Ituri 76.3% (10435/13685), weakest at Bunia 27.7% (1004/3620) and Nia-Nia 57.1% (220/385); Nord-Kivu 81.3% (14563/17923), with Manguredjipa 0.0% (0/215), Kyondo 53.0% (157/296) and Mabalako 58.5% (741/1267); Tshopo 82.8%, Haut-Uele 90.4%, Bas-Uele 93.0%. Only Sud-Ubangi (44/44) reaches 95%.

Alerts: 2651 of 2659 verified (99.7%), 458 validated as suspects, 450 investigated (98.3%) and 151 transferred (printed 33.6%, which is over the 450 investigated). The 8 unverified alerts and the 8 suspects not investigated are all in Ituri (Rwampara per the key messages); Sud-Ubangi prints ND.

PoE/PoC completeness 112/119 (94.1%): Sud-Kivu 55.6% (5/9) with no isolation at Kavimvira, Kalundu Port SNCC and Baraka; Nord-Kivu back to 95.2% (20/21) but the Butuhe PoC stays closed since the 26 September security incident, PoC alerts are handled late, providers on the Butembo axis are threatened, and communications, consumables and a dedicated ambulance are lacking; Ituri lacks supervision mobility at Rwampara, Nizi and Bunia, September provider pay is late, the Mandima PoCs need an ambulance and the Avakubi PoC is non-functional for insecurity; Haut-Uele's Matari PoC did not report for lack of a scheduled flight; Bas-Uele PNHF services are not functional and providers are untrained and unmotivated.

Ituri: 8 of 35 rings unopened, 13 of 58 households not decontaminated, 9 EDS failed and 14 of 79 bodies (17.7%) not swabbed; Nord-Kivu: ring gap at Katwa, weak household decontamination at Katwa and Kyondo, none of 10 decontaminated households received kits and 47 EDS postponed because families were not ready; Tshopo short of IPC supplies and IPC-trained frontline workers; Haut-Uele's Pawa CTE has no fence, a single latrine and too little cleaning equipment; Bas-Uele 16 of 20 priority facilities without functional triage, none with mattresses, 17 of 20 without 72-hour water storage and weak community death alert reporting.

Ituri: 393 patients at a printed 38% with no bed denominator, 45 critical; low capacity at Kilo, Lolwa and Biakato, imminent blood stock-out (6 units left), no food for 8 patients in Mandima (CT Mandima and CT Makeke), ambulance movement reporting 12/33.

Nord-Kivu: CTE/CT occupancy 349/410 (85.1%), suspect beds saturated at 92.7% (178/192) and 122 of 471 patients (26%) cared for outside CTE/CT; ambulance data completeness 50% (Musienene, Beni, Butembo and Kalunguta missing).

Haut-Uele: admissions and bed occupancy for 17 October not transmitted; no Starlink link at every CTE, unpaid staff, nutrition inputs (MUAC tapes, height boards, F75, F100, ready-to-use food) missing and water and power short at some CTEs. Tshopo: 19 patients for 36 beds (52.8%); 6 confirmed cases from Bafwasende lost to follow-up.
Bas-Uele has no ambulance for patient transfers, its standard CTE at HGR Buta is still under construction and IT kits are lacking.

Ituri's frontline-worker target remains to be redefined (the challenge prints 1120 vaccinated against a provisional 1000, while the actions report a cumulative 1260); Bas-Uele cold-chain units are not running, vaccine quantities are insufficient and funds are awaited; Tshopo has a 551-vaccinee gap between its Excel and DHIS2 databases and Bafwasende has not reported for four days; the Nord-Kivu team lacks 2 vehicles and 3 small tents, and ARKTEK vaccine transport remains to be confirmed. Vaccine logistics do not establish efficacy against Bundibugyo.

Nord-Kivu baseline assessments: at HGR Oicha, triage outside the secured circuit and open only until 17:00, no PPE, pedal bins or hygiene products, an unsecured Ebola circuit in the laboratory, suspect deliveries in the shared ward and no tracing plan for TB and HIV patients lost to follow-up; at HGR Kyondo, non-compliant triage, 13 of 33 maternity staff untrained in SONU B and CPNr, 25 of 205 staff (12.2%) trained in IPC and 50 staff exposed, 5 of them quarantined. Tshopo's central prison assessment found 121 adult malnutrition cases, a TB drug stock-out for a cohort of 16 patients, very poor waste management, no triage and 0 of 10 staff trained or vaccinated. Haut-Uele's free-care subsidy shortfall persists in the 7 most affected zones.

Ituri psychosocial coverage reaches 14 of 28 affected zones (50.0%); Mandima's data still do not come in and only 15 of the 41 latest confirmed cases (36.6%) were supported, with training planned for 18 and 19 October; Bas-Uele coverage is embryonic, with activities just starting at Viadana; in Haut-Uele only Isiro and Pawa reported.

Ituri community engagement reporting completeness is low (10 of 28 zones, 36%); Nord-Kivu received 372 of 650 expected community alerts (57.2%) and engaged 1266 of 4750 people (26.7%) in community actions.

Tshopo: community tensions and a swab refusal at Bafwasende, where aggression and threats against rapid-response teams block investigations around cases 65 to 70; Haut-Uele: the Wamba sub-coordination moved toward the Bolebole-Mambati resistance area and teams were refused access to a church in Isiro where alerts were reported; Ituri: the Avakubi PoC remains non-functional for insecurity.

Alerts (pages 4-5): Tableau 3 and the prose agree on 2659 alerts, 2651 verified (99.7%), 458 validated (17.3% of verified), 2193 invalidated (82.7%), 450 investigated (98.3%) and 151 transferred. Sud-Ubangi prints ND throughout and the prose names the other five provinces. The 8 unverified alerts are live Ituri alerts and the 8 uninvestigated suspects are in Ituri, matching the key messages (Rwampara). The printed 33.6% transfer rate is 151/450 (over investigated), while 151/458 is 33.0%; SR154 printed its transfer rate over validated suspects. Basis preserved, not repaired. The prose sentence ends 'CT/CT', apparently truncated.

Contacts: 80.0% is 28144/35162 (cover, prose and key messages, up from 79.1%). The six printed provincial rows sum exactly to the national totals. A Haut-Uele sub-figure of 79.3% (130/164) names no zone and is not attributed. Sud-Kivu and Nord-Ubangi print no contact data and none is derived.

Nord-Kivu (page 7): 471 hospitalized, 2 critical; 349 in CTE/CT for 410 beds (printed 85.1%), suspects 178/192 (92.7%) and confirmed 171/218 (78.4%); 122 in facilities that are not CTE/CT (printed 26%; 122/471 is 25.9%). 349+122=471 reconciles. The 85.1% is a CTE/CT-only rate and the census exceeds the bed count, so no all-census occupancy is inferred. Hot meals went to 177 confirmed and 194 suspects, which do not match the 171/178 split; not used.

Nord-Kivu stock flow: SR155 printed no Nord-Kivu census. SR155's national 916 minus its four printed provincial stocks (380+44+18+3) leaves 471, the same as SR156's printed 471, yet SR156 prints 50 admissions and 62 exits (471+50-62=459; 471-50+62 implies a start of 483). The SR155 residual is not a printed Nord-Kivu stock; not repaired.

Ituri care (page 7): 393 patients follows exactly from SR155's 380 plus 114 admissions minus 101 exits; the printed 38% is integer precision with no bed denominator and, unlike SR155 (139 confirmed, 241 suspects), no confirmed/suspect split; none is carried. Hot meals reached 374 of 382 patients (98%), a base that differs from the 393 census. The care panel counts 76 children under LNPE/SLM (11 CTE, 4 creche, 61 community) while the continuity-of-care section counts 79 (9, 6 and 64). Both preserved.

Haut-Uele care (page 7): 2 confirmed deaths at the Pawa CTE (matching Tableau 2) and 2 non-case exits; the panel says 39 confirmed cases remain hospitalized and that admissions and occupancy were not transmitted. SR155's 44 was a mixed confirmed and suspect census; 44-2-2=40 against the printed 39. The SMSPS section reports 5 non-cases leaving the Pawa CTE and a suspect child admitted at the Isiro CTE, against the care panel's 2 non-cases and no admission data. Tableau 2's 2 new Haut-Uele confirmations (Isiro, Wamba) do not appear as admissions. Not repaired.

Tshopo care (page 7): 18+2-1=19 reconciles, 19/36 is the printed 52.8%; the two admissions are suspects while Tableau 2 gives two new Tshopo confirmations (Kabondo, Makiso-Kisangani), and no confirmed/suspect split is printed. 6 confirmed cases from Bafwasende are lost to follow-up (SR155: 7). Since the start, 44 confirmed cases received experimental treatment (3 MBP134, 41 remdesivir) and 464 people post-exposure prophylaxis (SR155: 42 and 457); neither is an efficacy signal.

Isolation: the cover 925 equals the five provincial stocks 393+471+39+19+3; Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Tshopo and Bas-Uele print no confirmed/suspect split, so no national split is derived. Ituri, Tshopo and Bas-Uele follow from SR155 plus same-day flows; Haut-Uele (40 vs 39) and Nord-Kivu (no SR155 stock) do not.

PoE/PoC (page 5): Tableau 4 covers Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Tshopo and Haut-Uele and the prose agrees: 5 alerts, 3 validated live suspects of which 2 transferred or referred (66.7%; one Ituri suspect refused transfer), 1 body intercepted and swabbed in Sud-Kivu, 1 Haut-Uele alert invalidated. Completeness 112/119 (94.1%) and 283178 travellers sum from the provinces. The Haut-Uele challenge names the Matari PoC as not reporting while its alert came from the Mutowamba PoC. No case is inferred.

Laboratory (page 6): 411 samples, 40 positive (9.7%), split 31 living and 9 deceased; deceased positives match Tableau 2's community deaths in every province and every printed provincial positivity matches its counts.
Key messages (page 10) agree with Tableau 3 and the prose on 450/458 investigated and 8 uninvestigated in Ituri, and on contact follow-up rising from 79.1% to 80.0%.

Vaccination (pages 7-8): Ituri's actions report a cumulative 1260 frontline workers vaccinated (515 women, 745 men), while the challenge still prints 1120 vaccinated against a provisional target of 1000 (SR155 printed a cumulative 1120). Both preserved; no winner chosen. Nord-Kivu vaccinated 130 for a cumulative 192 of 7105 (2.7%), which is SR155's 62 plus 130. Haut-Uele reaches 589 (470 Isiro, 80 Pawa, 39 Wamba; SR155 printed 588). Ituri reports continued research on Ervebo efficacy against BDBV; no efficacy signal is inferred.

SMSPS (page 9): Ituri prints 23 of 44 confirmed cases supported and its challenge 15 of the 41 latest confirmed cases; 44 is SR155's Ituri daily count and 41 SR154's, not SR156's 27. The challenge's 'Mandima concentrates 51% of cases' fits SR154 (21/41, 51.2%) and roughly SR156 (14/27, 51.9%). Nord-Kivu's 12 of 14 latest confirmed cases matches SR155's 14, not SR156's 9; Haut-Uele prints 1 new confirmed case against Tableau 2's 2. Not repaired.
